title: Universal epimorphic covers and finite quasi-compact cover calculus
statement:
Let $\mathcal E$ be a Grothendieck topos, presented as sheaves of sets on a small site, with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention] and quasi-compactness as in [def-trf-coherent-topos]. A family $(f_i:X_i\to Y)_{i\in I}$ is jointly epimorphic when its coproduct map $\coprod_iX_i\to Y$ is an epimorphism; epimorphism means right cancellation against all objects. All families below are small in the containing universe. Then:
(1) The family is jointly epimorphic if and only if every section of $Y$ locally lifts through one of the $f_i$: on a covering of its site object, its restrictions are images of sections of individual $X_i$, with the index allowed to vary on the covering. For every $Z\to Y$, the family $(X_i\times_Y Z\to Z)_i$ is jointly epimorphic whenever $(f_i)_i$ is. In particular epimorphisms are stable under pullback. If $(X_i\to B)_i$ and $(Y_j\to C)_j$ are jointly epimorphic and $B,C\to A$ are any maps, then $(X_i\times_A Y_j\to B\times_A C)_{i,j}$ is jointly epimorphic.
(2) For an epimorphism $e:X\to Y$, quasi-compactness of $X$ implies quasi-compactness of $Y$.
(3) Every finite coproduct of quasi-compact objects is quasi-compact, including the empty coproduct. Consequently, if an object admits a finite jointly epimorphic family from quasi-compact objects, it is quasi-compact.

Tag 00WN (lemma-mono-epi-sheaves), Tag 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf), Tag 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), Tag 0GMP (lemma-image-of-quasi-compact), Tag 0GMQ (lemma-coproduct-quasi-compact). Local lifting and universal jointly epimorphic families are the sheaf-theoretic expansion; the empty coproduct case is included explicitly.

proof.text: Work on the small site presenting $\mathcal E$, with all site data, section sets and index sets in the containing universe of the statement. For the family $(X_i)_i$ form the presheaf $P(U)=\coprod_i X_i(U)$, whose restrictions preserve the index. Its sheafification $P^\#$ is the coproduct in sheaves: a natural transformation $P\to H$ to a sheaf is exactly a family of natural transformations $X_i\to H$, and by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] it extends uniquely to $P^\#\to H$. Thus the map $p:\coprod_iX_i\to Y$ is induced by $(i,x)\mapsto f_i(x)$. This proves the required coproduct identification directly from the universal property, for arbitrary small $I$, including $I=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 00WB (theorem-plus), universal property of sheafification; coproduct identification proved directly from the adjunction of def-weil-pbc-sheafification.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective], $p$ is epic exactly when sections of $Y$ locally lift to $P^\#$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], each such lifted section is, on a further covering, represented by an element $(i,x)$ of $P$. Composing the two site coverings gives local lifts through individual $f_i$, with the index varying between covering objects. Conversely, local lifts through the $f_i$ map into $P^\#$ and make $p$ locally surjective, hence epic by the same epimorphism criterion. Coverings compose by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1)(ii). The sheafification lemma applies because our common containing universe contains the objects and morphisms of the small site, as well as all values of $P$.

For $Z\to Y$, a section $z\in Z(U)$ has image $y\in Y(U)$. Step 2 gives, locally, $x\in X_i$ with $f_i(x)=y$. By the sectionwise pullback description in [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise], the pair $(x,z)$ is a section of $X_i\times_Y Z$ lifting $z$. Step 2 makes the pulled-back family jointly epic. Taking a singleton proves pullback stability of epimorphisms. For the product assertion, a section $(b,c)$ of $B\times_A C$ first locally lifts $b$ to some $x_i$, and on each resulting covering object locally lifts $c$ to some $y_j$. On that further cover the images of $x_i,y_j$ in $A$ agree because they equal the restrictions of the images of $b,c$. Hence $(x_i,y_j)$ is a section of $X_i\times_A Y_j$ lifting $(b,c)$. The composite is a covering by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1)(ii), so step 2 proves joint epimorphy. This proves all of clause (1).

source.place: Tag 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf), pullbacks; Tag 00VH (definition-site), composition of coverings; elementary local-lifting argument.

proof.text: For clause (2), let $(T_j\to Y)_{j\in J}$ be a jointly epic family and let $e:X\to Y$ be epic with $X$ quasi-compact. Step 3 makes $(X\times_Y T_j\to X)_j$ jointly epic. The definition in [def-trf-coherent-topos] supplies a finite $J_0\subset J$ for which the corresponding coproduct map $q:\coprod_{j\in J_0}(X\times_Y T_j)\to X$ is epic. To check that the selected $(T_j\to Y)_{j\in J_0}$ are jointly epic, take any $a,b:Y\to H$ agreeing on each selected $T_j$. The pullback equations give $aeq=beq$, and right cancellation first of $q$ and then of $e$ gives $a=b$. By the coproduct universal property this is exactly epimorphy of $\coprod_{j\in J_0}T_j\to Y$. Every jointly epic family of $Y$ therefore has a finite jointly epic subfamily.

source.place: Tag 0GMP (lemma-image-of-quasi-compact), part (2); omitted proof expanded using clause (1) and right cancellation.

proof.text: For clause (3), let $I$ be finite, with each $X_i$ quasi-compact, and put $S=\coprod_{i\in I}X_i$. Given a jointly epic family $(T_j\to S)_{j\in J}$, pull it back to each $X_i$ by step 3. By [def-trf-coherent-topos], choose a finite $J_i\subset J$ such that $(X_i\times_S T_j\to X_i)_{j\in J_i}$ is jointly epic. The union $J_0=\bigcup_{i\in I}J_i$ is finite. If $a,b:S\to H$ agree on $T_j$ for all $j\in J_0$, they agree after each of the jointly epic pulled-back families indexed by $J_i$, hence on $X_i$ for every $i$. The coproduct universal property gives $a=b$, proving that $(T_j\to S)_{j\in J_0}$ is jointly epic. If $I=\varnothing$, use $J_0=\varnothing$: the map from the empty subfamily is $0\to S=0$, an isomorphism and therefore epic by right cancellation. Thus the initial sheaf is quasi-compact as well; no pointwise emptiness of this sheaf is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0GMQ (lemma-coproduct-quasi-compact); omitted proof expanded, including the additional empty-coproduct case via its universal property.

proof.text: Finally, a finite jointly epic family $(X_i\to Y)_{i\in I}$ of quasi-compact objects gives an epimorphism $\coprod_iX_i\to Y$ by the definition of joint epimorphy. Its source is quasi-compact by step 5 and its target is quasi-compact by step 4. This also applies when $I=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tags 0GMP (lemma-image-of-quasi-compact) and 0GMQ (lemma-coproduct-quasi-compact), immediate combination of the two proved clauses.

The statement is unchanged from live, the item is still unsplit in the live and side-live clones, the delivery creates no new nodes, and proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses. Step 1 builds the sheaf coproduct as the sheafification of the presheaf disjoint union, using the universal property in def-weil-pbc-sheafification. Step 2 proves 'epi iff sections locally lift through a single f_i': the epi lemma gives local lifts, the sections-local lemma represents each by θ(i,x), and coverings compose by axiom (1)(ii); the universe hypothesis of the sections-local lemma is covered by the item's containing universe. Step 3 proves the pullback and product clauses with the finite-limit case of the sectionwise limit lemma, lifting first on one covering and then on a further one. Step 4 proves Stacks 0GMP(2): pull back to X, choose finite J0 from def-trf-coherent-topos, then cancel q and e. Step 5 proves Stacks 0GMQ: take a finite J_i for each summand, use the union, and apply the coproduct property; the empty coproduct is handled correctly, which goes beyond the source's n≥1. Step 6 combines steps 4 and 5. Read sites.tex 0GMP and 0GMQ (both proofs omitted) and definition-quasi-compact-topos. Tested Sets, an identity epi, X=0, an empty family and an empty covering. Searched the DAG for 0GMP, 0GMQ and 'jointly epimorphic'; the closest nodes (sheaf-quasicompact-coproduct-calculus, site-epimorphic-family-cover-lifts, lifted-generator-quasiseparated-test) do not duplicate the item.
